newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 rice exports to remain strong - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 rice exports to remain strong - ministry.

text.p: Thailand's rice exports for 1997 are expected to remain strong due to a drop in production from India and delayed harvests in Vietnam, a senior commerce ministry official said on Wednesday.
But other major exports such as tapioca and rubber could face tougher times due to a grain surplus in the European Union and generally high rubber stocks.
Pracha Charutrakulchai, head of the ministry foreign trade department, said the ministry set a rice export target for next year of 5.0 million tonnes against 5.2 million projected for this year.
The minimum rice export value for 1997 was seen at 40 billion baht ($1.6 million), he said.
"Despite expected good global rice output and high Thai prices, the exports will remain good next year because of problems in major exporting countries such as India and Vietnam," he said.
Pracha said floods in India were likely to reduce its exports to 1.8 million tonnes in 1997 from more than three million tonnes this year.
Storms in Vietnam had also forced that country to delay its harvests and supplies would not be available until March.
"We will be able to sell well from now until end-February," he said.
Pracha expressed concerns over the competitiveness of Thai medium- and low-quality rice as the same quality rice was sold at lower prices by Vietnam and India.
However, he said the government was encouraging farmers to produce more quality rice, a market dominated by Thailand.
Asia would remain a major market for Thailand with China, Singapore and Malaysia as key buyers, Pracha said.
The agriculture ministry forecast that 1996/97 (April-March) rice production would drop to 21.259 million tonnes from 22.015 million the previous season.
The output from the first crop was forecast at 17.759 million tonnes and the second crop at 3.50 million tonnes.
